name: Opus 5 vol regime
strategy: High-vol regime defense: net-flat low-beta versus high-beta spread (long consumer staples XLP and a trimmed integrated-energy XLE sleeve against a short in small caps IWM), with 50% cash at 4% until equity vol mean-reverts.
reassessment_note: Last week's book assumed the early-November equity-vol spike had faded and leaned mid-vol (net +5% long, SPY long against IWM short). That premise has broken. VIX rose about 11% to 25.46 on 11-17, then jumped 26% to 35.89 on 11-20 as the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and XLK fell 9% in one session (tapeboard market pulse 11-17 and 11-20). That ended a five-session slide of roughly 8.6% on SPY. The 10-year yield has eased from about 5.1% to 4.91%, and WTI is firm near $84. The book held up (-0.53% NAV) only because the IWM short offset the longs. The SPY long is -6.78%, sitting 0.2% from its -7% stop, and SPY is now a concentrated bet on the tech and AI complex at the epicentre of the selloff. A vol-regime mandate in a VIX-35 regime should not carry index beta, so I drop SPY. I keep the short-beta side and swap the long leg into low-vol defensives: XLP was the best sector on 11-20 at -0.79%. I trim XLE from 15% to 10% because oil is firm but energy equities still trade with the tape. Net exposure is about 0% and gross is 50%. Stops are widened modestly for the higher daily range, so routine noise does not knock out the hedge legs. I re-risk only when VIX falls back below about 25. Research was a few web searches and fetches; some news results were from 2025 and I disregarded them.

positions.thesis: Kept at 25% as the core short-beta leg. Small caps are high-beta and margin- and refinancing-sensitive. The Russell fell 2.76% on 11-20, with speculative crypto-linked names down 17-18%, and in a VIX-36 regime that risk-off rotation tends to persist. The stop is widened to 10% because a capitulation relief rally after five straight down days is the main risk to this leg. The XLP and XLE longs offset part of that risk.

Replaces the SPY long. Consumer staples are the lowest-beta, least tech-exposed sector and held best on 11-20 (-0.79% against -3.7% for the S&P). Easing 10-year yields (5.1% to 4.91%) also help bond-proxy defensives. Long XLP against short IWM is a low-vol-minus-high-beta spread, which is the factor that pays in a high-vol regime, and it does not depend on calling the bottom. Sized at 15% so the book stays roughly net flat with the energy sleeve.

Trimmed from 15% to 10%. Integrated energy has little exposure to the AI-capex unwind, and WTI is holding around $83-85 while the tape falls, which supports cash flows. But XLE still fell about 5% from entry with the market (-1.27% on 11-20), so its diversification is partial and it deserves a smaller weight in a high-vol regime. The stop is at 9% from the new entry to allow for elevated daily ranges.
